Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 44-year-old male presents with 5 days of dry cough, runny nose, muscle aches, and mild headache/chills; viral upper respiratory infection suspected.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dry cough (~5 days), runny nose, muscle aches, occasional headache, and chills.
- No hemoptysis, no shortness of breath, no wheeze, no chest discomfort.
- Home management: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented). No ibuprofen.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (5–6 years), hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented), Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Blood sugars: Self-monitored; within normal range.
- Blood pressure: Taken this morning; within normal range (exact values not provided).
- No allergies documented.
- Social history/preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Mild redness at the back of throat.
- No enlarged tonsils.
- No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy.
- Vitals: Not documented.

Impression:
- Viral upper respiratory tract infection.

Plan:
- Supportive management: Continue current symptomatic relief.
- May use Night Nurse/Day Nurse (compatible with current medications).
- Monitor for worsening symptoms: Shortness of breath, wheeze, symptoms persisting >3 weeks, or deterioration—re-contact provider if present.
- No prescription required at present.
- No need for further examination or intervention at this time.

Quality checks:

●	Missing clinically expected elements: Allergies not documented; medication doses/routes/frequencies not specified; no details on smoking/alcohol or vaccination status.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear and complete for main clinical information; minor conversational fillers present.
